Deployment types: in-place (update instances in turn; EC2 and on-premises) and blue/greenBlue/green deploymentReleasing a new version (green) alongside the running one (blue), then moving traffic to green once it is ready. Rolling back is quick: move the traffic back to blue.Glossary entryClose (create a new set of instances, tasks, or a new function version, then move traffic).

Deployment configurations: for EC2, how many instances stay healthy (CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime is the default, HalfAtATime, AllAtOnce, or custom). For Lambda and ECS, how traffic shifts: canary (for example CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes: 10% first, the rest after 5 minutes), linear (for example LambdaLinear10PercentEvery1Minute), or all at once.
AppSpec file: what to deploy and lifecycle hooks, such as running a validation Lambda function before and after traffic shifts.

Automatic rollback when a deployment fails or a CloudWatch alarm (for example on error rate or latencyLatencyThe time between sending a request and receiving the response, usually measured in milliseconds. Distance and processing add to it; caching and serving users from nearby locations reduce it.Glossary entryClose) goes into alarm.
10% of traffic first, the rest later→ leads to Canary configuration
10% more every minute→ leads to Linear configuration
Lambda or ECS inference service→ leads to CodeDeploy blue/green
Roll back when errors rise→ leads to Alarm-based automatic rollback
Run tests before traffic moves→ leads to AppSpec lifecycle hook
SageMaker AI endpoint update→ leads to Deployment guardrails
CodeDeploy deploys to EC2, on-premises, Lambda, and ECS with in-place or blue/green deployments.
Lambda and ECS support canary, linear, and all-at-once traffic shifting; EC2 configurations keep a minimum of healthy hosts.
AppSpec hooks run checks; CloudWatch alarms trigger automatic rollback.
For SageMaker AI endpoints, use deployment guardrails instead.

AWS CodeDeploy automates deployments to Amazon EC2 instances, on-premisesOn-premisesIn data centers or offices that you run yourself, rather than in the cloud. Hybrid architectures connect on-premises systems to AWS, for example through AWS Direct Connect or a VPN.Glossary entryClose servers, AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon ECS services. It controls how a new version replaces the old one, shifts traffic gradually where the platform allows, runs your checks at each step, and rolls back automatically when a deployment fails or an alarm fires.

Choose CodeDeploy when a question asks to release a new version of an application or a Lambda- or ECS-based inference service with canary or linear traffic shifting and automatic rollback (MLA-C02 tasks 3.3.1 and 3.3.2). For models on SageMaker AI endpoints, use SageMaker AI's own deployment guardrails instead.
CodeDeploy uses a service role; EC2 instances need an instance profile and the CodeDeploy agent; revisions in S3 are encrypted; CloudTrail logs deployments.
Blue/green keeps the old version ready for fast rollback; alarm-based rollback limits the damage of a bad release.
Canary and linear shifting limit how many users see a new version at once; choose the step size and interval to match how quickly problems show up.
No extra charge for deployments to EC2, Lambda, or ECS; on-premises deployments are charged per instance update. You pay for the resources created, such as a second fleet during blue/green.
Deployment state changes go to EventBridge and SNS; CloudWatch alarms drive rollback; the console shows each lifecycle event.
